findings.title: Missing sink in split-K receipt instance
findings.full_text: **F1 — CLOSED (original severity MAJOR): S3 omitted the receipt’s sink.** The amendment adds exp(sink) exactly once to the denominator, with no numerator contribution, and uses sink=0 in both outputs of the required >0.8 conjunct. Universal containment and the earlier sink-free gap are retained. Evidence: Spec 54–58, 94–107; Proofs 194–249; SP1.1 report 9–13; receipt test 67–74; reference 37–50; passing Lean probe and independent operand recomputation. Proposed restatement, now implemented: retain containment and require both the sink-0 and sink-free gaps for bulk [2,0], exact [2,10], V [0,1], δ=0 and singleton partitions. Prior art: SP1.1 R26 (2026), standard softmax sink normalization; review only, no new algorithm.
findings.proposed_restatement: Retain universal containment and require both sink-0 and sink-free >0.8 gaps on original operands.
findings.prior_art: SP1.1 R26 (2026), standard softmax sink normalization; no new algorithm.

findings.title: Non-vacuity witness missed the antecedent
findings.full_text: **F2 — CLOSED (original severity MINOR): S2’s witness missed its antecedent.** The amended conjunction requires an existential with finalRefined true and retains the strictness existential. Its positive witness is bulk [0,1], δ=0, key 1: rowMax=prefixMax=1, so finalRefined and spRefined both hold. Key 0 still witnesses strict containment. Evidence: Spec 81–87; Proofs 148–171; Check 15–16; independent Lean evaluation. Proposed restatement, now implemented: (∃ b δ j, finalRefined b δ j) ∧ (∃ b δ j, spRefined b δ j ∧ ¬finalRefined b δ j). Prior art: REV1 F2 (2026), SP1 R24 (2026), BLASST’s running-max criterion; review only, no new algorithm.
findings.proposed_restatement: Conjoin an existential finalRefined witness with the existing strictness existential.

witnesses.instance: bulk=[1,0], delta=0, j=1: 0<1 is an active skip.
witnesses.attack: A one-key delta=0 row has no skip and would make an implication vacuous. The actual witness has two keys. A separate [2,1,3], j=1, k=2 instance exercises a strictly later prefix (Lean-checked).

witnesses.instance: bulk=[0,1], delta=0; j=1 final-refines and prefix-refines; j=0 prefix-refines but does not final-refine.
witnesses.attack: Strictness alone makes the main implication antecedent false at j=0. New first conjunct and the independently evaluated j=1 witness close that hole.

witnesses.instance: bulk=[2,0], delta=0, P={0}, j=0 is a member and is globally refined. Output construction is fixed, without a conditional antecedent.
witnesses.attack: P=univ makes containment equality and could hide a reversed inequality. Separate bulk=[2,0,1], P={1,2}, j=1 gives local prefix 0<global prefix 2. Lean checks local=0. V=0 would make output equality trivial; actual V=[0,1] and changed second score avoid this.

witnesses.instance: z=0 lies in [0,sqrt 3]. The same pair is checked at z=sqrt 3 as well.
witnesses.attack: Contradictory z bounds would vacuate the universal claim. z=0 and sqrt 3 satisfy actual bounds. A=[1,0,0,0] has threshold (1+z sqrt 3)/4, at most 1 on the interval; B=[1,0,0,10] has mean 11/4>1 and nonnegative added term. Same first input 1 forces any f to the same decision.

witnesses.instance: bulk=[10,0], exact=[9,1], errq=1, epsilon=1/2, j=1. Both errors are exactly 1; delta=log 2+2<=3, so 0<10-delta is an active skip.
witnesses.attack: epsilon>1 could make the weight bound trivial. Actual witness uses epsilon=1/2 and satisfies every-key error bound and skip together; independent Lean evaluation checks all premises.

quantifier_and_scope_checks: S1: nonempty inclusive prefixes, signed bulk, strict skip from negating an inclusive refine threshold; same skipped key is compared with every later prefix and final max. All real margins remain quantified.
S2: finalRefined implies spRefined, not equality of masks or outputs. Antecedent and strictness witnesses are separate existentials; they need not be the same key.

S3: arbitrary finite P containing j generalizes ordered partition containment; P intersect the inclusive global prefix contains j, so there is no empty-maximum default. No partition-cover hypothesis is needed for the per-key order result. The fixed output comparison uses a genuine covering pair of singletons and one sink after aggregation.
S4: for each fixed z in [0,sqrt 3], the common first prefix cannot support irrevocable agreement on both rows. This is not an impossibility with unrestricted buffering or a claim for every real z.

S5: every key has bounded bulk/exact error. Nonempty row implies errq>=0 from that premise. epsilon>0 is sufficient; allowing epsilon>1 generalizes the receipt without weakening it. The strict skipped-key conclusion concerns true weights, not bulk or mixed weights. A common positive softmax denominator (including an unchanged sink) cancels. No aggregate error or empirical universal quantization bound is asserted.
